instantiation.worst_case: hello is an internal gRPC service that today nobody may call: its only AuthorizationPolicy is `allow-nothing` (spec: {}), so every caller is denied. This change opens exactly one method, /hello.v1.HelloService/Hello, to exactly one mTLS identity. Worst case if the generated identifiers are wrong: frontend's calls are denied and frontend's end-to-end test fails — no user-visible failure, because frontend serves no inbound traffic (sum(rate(istio_requests_total{destination_service_namespace="frontend"}[1h])) returns no data) and neither service is reachable from outside the cluster (only ClusterIP Services; no ingress gateway anywhere in the fleet). Worst case if they are too broad: an unintended workload inside namespace frontend gains the right to call one side-effect-free method whose request is a name string and whose response is "hello <name>" — no credentials, no financial or health data. Worst case if hello cannot carry the load: hello runs ONE ready replica in the only observable cluster with a KEDA ceiling of 2, so a traffic spike sheds with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; the only thing degraded is frontend. The blast radius is one request path on an internal service with no human users behind it, so the bar is reduced — except for correct, available and secure, which the properties hold at full regardless because this is a manifest change that grants access.

proposals.content:
# Identifiers and stack binding for smallStepGiantLeap/hello.
# Derived at review of pull request #1 (head 9050549d2e78); the repository had
# no such file. Identifiers only: no endpoints, hostnames or secrets.
# Each stack line carries a check that re-verifies it on the next run.
version: 1

workloads:
  hello:
    namespace: hello
    selector: app=hello
    container: hello
    kind: argoproj.io/v1alpha1/Rollout
    name: hello
    service_account: hello
    principal: cluster.local/ns/hello/sa/hello
    ports:
      grpc: 50051
      metrics: 9090
    image: ghcr.io/smallstepgiantleap/hello
    metric_families:
      - vikrant_inflight_rpcs
      - vikrant_rpcs_handled_total
      - vikrant_unary_latency_seconds
      - vikrant_rejected_total
      - vikrant_build_info
    environments:
      dev:
        overlay: deploy/envs/dev
        clusters: [e1-dev]
      staging:
        overlay: deploy/envs/staging
        clusters: []   # the overlay exists; the fleet knows no staging cluster (see q3)
      prod:
        overlay: deploy/envs/prod
        clusters: [e1-prod]

callers:
  frontend:
    repo: smallStepGiantLeap/frontend
    namespace: frontend
    selector: app=frontend
    service_account: frontend
    principal: cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend
    methods:
      - hello.v1.HelloService/Hello
    note: >-
      namespace frontend also runs a Deployment named `traffic` with the same
      service account and the same app=frontend label; it is the source of all
      observed calls to hello. See q4.

stack:
  mesh:
    is: istio 1.31.1, sidecar injection, STRICT mTLS
    check: >-
      istio_build{component="pilot"} reports tag 1.31.1 and every
      istio_requests_total{destination_service_namespace="hello"} series
      carries connection_security_policy="mutual_tls"
  gitops:
    is: argo-cd, control plane in namespace argocd
    check: kube_pod_info{namespace="argocd"} returns a running argocd-application-controller pod
    unknown: >-
      no argocd_* metric family is exported and no Application manifest was
      found in this repository, so the tracked revision is unverified. See q1.
  progressive_delivery:
    is: argo-rollouts, canary with an AnalysisTemplate on server-error ratio
    check: kube_replicaset_owner{namespace="hello"} returns owner_kind="Rollout", owner_name="hello"
    note: >-
      applies to pod-template revisions only; policy and access changes in
      deploy/base reach every environment at once.
  autoscaler:
    is: keda, ScaledObject hello scaling the Rollout on sum(vikrant_inflight_rpcs)
    check: kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_info{namespace="hello",horizontalpodautoscaler="keda-hpa-hello"} exists
  admission:
    is: pod security admission at enforce=restricted; webhooks are istio and keda only, no general policy engine
    check: kube_namespace_labels{namespace="hello"} carries label_pod_security_kubernetes_io_enforce="restricted"
  network_policy:
    is: plain kubernetes NetworkPolicy
    check: kube_networkpolicy_spec_ingress_rules{namespace="hello",networkpolicy="default-deny"} exists
  metrics:
    is: prometheus-compatible, scraping kube-state-metrics, envoy sidecar stats and the service's vikrant_* instrumentation
    check: vikrant_build_info{namespace="hello"} returns a series
    gap: no cAdvisor family exists, so container CPU and memory usage cannot be measured
  alerting:
    is: none
    check: metrics_rules() returns an empty groups list

documents:
  - README.md

answers: {}
proposals.reason: The repository had no .paved-agent/discover.yaml, so every identifier and every stack line in this review was derived from scratch. Recording them makes the next review cheaper and lets each line be re-verified by its check rather than re-discovered. The stack is named from what was found — Istio 1.31.1, Argo CD, Argo Rollouts, KEDA, Pod Security admission, a Prometheus-compatible backend with no rules — never assumed. The gaps (no staging cluster, no argocd_* metrics, no cAdvisor, no alert rules) are recorded as gaps rather than left blank, and the four open questions are keyed to the `answers:` block they will fill.

summary: Ships, with eyes open. The grant itself is correct and least-privilege: the generated principal cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend, the namespace label and the pod label app=frontend all match frontend exactly — confirmed both in its manifests and live in the mesh — the path is the only method on the proto and exactly what frontend declared in egress, all 38 platform-owned files verify against the stamp, the data is a name string over STRICT mTLS, and three new end-to-end checks prove reach, identity-based denial and survival of a node drain in a real Istio kind cluster. Two things should be seen before merging. First, this pull request is not the gate it appears to be: both objects are already live in e1-prod and frontend is already calling successfully at about 6 rps, which contradicts the description's "until then frontend's calls are denied" and means the access was granted ahead of review — and with no argocd_* metrics I could not establish what that cluster is reconciling. Second, nothing is watching: the metrics backend evaluates zero alert rules, so a failure of this grant would be silent, and hello runs a single replica with a ceiling of 2 in the cluster labelled prod against a prod overlay declaring 3 and 3/10. Load is a non-issue — four orders of magnitude of headroom against an O(1) handler. Four yes/no questions are attached, and a .paved-agent/discover.yaml is proposed since none existed.
